players.product: physics-plus-AI molecular discovery platform and Bunsen co-scientist

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Richie Jain on the hosted transition: the move from on-prem to hosted runs over a three-year period from a starting point of 'about 25% hosted' on software revenue toward a 75% goal; hosted at 47% in Q2 was 'ahead of where we expected to be at this point', with large customers transitioned ahead of renewal dates. He said hosting gives a cleaner financial profile (ratable recognition), insight into how customers use the technology and a better position at renewals. CTO of Software Pat Lorton said customers showed 'essentially no resistance whatsoever.'
quarterly_data.figure: starting point about 25% hosted; goal 75%; Q2 47% hosted, ahead of expectations

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ramy Farid: Schrödinger is 'very serious about our goal of achieving breakeven profitability on an adjusted EBITDA basis by 2028', to be reached primarily by growing while managing expenses with discipline. CFO Richie Jain said operating expenses through the first half of the year are down about 6% (headcount reductions and lower professional services and therapeutics CRO spending, the full-year annualization of last year's actions) and that the company is focused on getting to profitability on an operating basis while building milestones, royalties and equity positions like Tectora for further upside.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA breakeven target by 2028; first-half opex down about 6%

quarterly_data.signal: President of R&D Karen Akinsanya: having decided last year not to take programs into the clinic, Schrödinger moves programs through discovery and then partners them; the Tectora spin-out of two immunology programs 'raised $55 million', which will fund them through discovery and, it hopes, into early clinical development, taking that CRO cost off Schrödinger's balance sheet. Schrödinger holds 'a pretty significant equity stake' and Tectora is 'I think our eighth new co' under the Schrödinger umbrella. She said the more than $750 million realized combines upfronts, milestones, royalties and cash distributions from sales of co-founded biotechs or their assets - Nimbus asset sales and the acquisitions of Morphic, Petra and Ajax.
quarterly_data.figure: Tectora raised $55 million; eighth newco; $750 million realized

quarterly_data.signal: President of R&D Karen Akinsanya on Novartis: after portfolio prioritization decisions at Novartis in the last couple of quarters, Schrödinger 'will be reshuffling the deck there a little bit in terms of the targets' in the significant partnership signed with Novartis a couple of years ago; 'We don't think there's a major impact', and the economics will be looked at in the third quarter. She named BMS, Lilly and Novartis among Schrödinger's partners and said collaboration demand 'continues to be really high'.

CFO Richie Jain: materials science is 'about 10% of our business today'; the demand backdrop on September 14 is 'just incredibly stronger' than a year ago across big pharma, biotech and materials science, a trend he expects to continue into Q4, which is generally more than 50% of the year; and 'our largest collaboration partners are also our largest software customers.' CEO Ramy Farid said the top 20 pharma have been customers for decades, an adoption gap remains between the largest and smaller customers, and the reopening biotech market should benefit Schrödinger.
quarterly_data.figure: materials science about 10% of business; Q4 more than 50% of the year

quarterly_data.signal: On products and AI: CTO of Software Pat Lorton said interest in the Bunsen agent exceeds any product he has seen in 20 years at Schrödinger, that pharma AI budgets are going to Schrödinger rather than away from it ('we're pulling money out of AI budgets'), that Schrödinger uses AI coding tools heavily to build products faster, and that LiveDesign for Biologics, introduced in the last year, is catching on at several big pharma. CEO Ramy Farid said Schrödinger rolled out Predictive Tox and Crystal Structure Prediction this year alongside Bunsen, reaching budgets it had not accessed before, and that physics simulation generates 'about 10 years' worth of experimental data in one day' (company claim). President of R&D Karen Akinsanya said Predictive Tox beta testing came back significantly positive and customers are now incorporating it into workflows.

connects_to.relationship: enterprise deployment of Bunsen and molecular discovery software

contracts.signal: CEO Ramy Farid on the BMS Bunsen agreement: BMS, a longstanding partner, got access to 'a significant amount of the technology, more throughput', so it can predict the properties of more molecules computationally; the deal 'involved the AI budgets', the computational people and BD, and he called it 'a big strategic partnership'.
